To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
students can be successfully transitioned from face to face to online learning with minimal disruption to their engagement and success.

(1) students can quickly adapt to online teaching and learning environments, (2) students who engage in a range of online learning activities, such as watching lecture recordings, participating in online tutorials and discussion forums, and completing low stakes assessment, are more likely to succeed, and (3) the impact of engagement on success was lower for online tutorials, compared to face to face tutorials, but was otherwise similar.
student engagement in low stakes assessments, discussion forum participation, and tutorial attendance are associated with success in first year chemistry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transition to online learning, but also the transition of students from secondary school to tertiary study.
the transition to online learning in first year chemistry and the role of student engagement as a predictor of success in this transition.
the transition to emergency online learning and how student engagement can be used to predict success in the online environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the online environment is a viable option to deliver first year chemistry, and that student engagement is a strong predictor of success in both face to face and online environments.
engagement is important for success, and that this is the case whether learning is online or face to face.
engagement with the course is a strong predictor of success in first year chemistry, and that this is not affected by the mode of delivery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the students were able to successfully transition to an online learning environment, and that the level of engagement was a strong predictor of success in both the online and face to face environments.

students were able, and willing, to engage in the learning activities provided, with the exception of tutorials, and that engagement with the learning activities was associated with success, irrespective of whether the unit was taught face to face, or online.
engagement in the online transition was similar to the previous offering and that the level of engagement was a significant predictor of success in the online environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students are willing and capable of engaging with online learning activities, and that this engagement is associated with success in the course.
students are able to quickly adapt and engage in online learning, and that this engagement is a strong predictor of success in the course.

the online environment provides opportunities for students to engage with learning in ways that are not possible in a face to face environment, with the potential for this to improve their overall experience and success.
